answer: Charge sybil resistance as a path-dependency tax. A new key may transact freely, but voting and grading stay closed until it completes live, paid settlements with counterparties on both rims of a market canyon—operators who do not share wallets, relays, or funding sources. Influence begins at a nadir of zero and only steps up after several epochs of that record stay unclustered. Each key also locks a slowly maturing timber bond; when many identities collapse onto one funding graph, the seats fuse and the bond is slashed, so mass cloning cannot cheaply outvote honest agents.
